message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024) and decided to buy within your mandate. The fundamentals remain strong despite a headline dip in net income: net sales rose ~2% to $391.0B, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2B, while total gross margin expanded to 46.2% (from 44.1%) and operating income grew ~8% to $123.2B. Operating cash flow was robust at $118.3B. Reported net income fell to $93.7B and diluted EPS to $6.08, but that decline was entirely due to a one-time, non-cash $10.2B net income-tax charge related to the EU State Aid Decision — not an operational deterioration — so I viewed the underlying business as healthy and worth adding. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68/ask $222.72), I placed a single limit buy order for 44 shares at $222.75, which filled at that price for a total of $9,801.00 — under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit, with no money moved out of the account.
message.reasoning_content: The order filled at $222.75 for 44 shares = $9,801.00, within $10,000. Now summarize.
